html:
The Pacamoros, also called Bracamoros, were peoples of the eastern Andean slopes on today's border between Ecuador and Peru, around the Chinchipe River and Jaén. Their language is lost, and little is known of them as a group.

The Inca armies are said to have failed to conquer this rough forest country. In the 1540s and 1550s Spanish captains founded towns here to mine gold, but many were later abandoned. Their neighbours included the Paltas in the highlands and the Awajún in the forest.

The same valley holds one of the oldest finds of the Americas: traces at Santa Ana-La Florida show that people there used cacao more than 5,000 years ago.
